title: Microflow cataloguer + synthesizer for executable admin flows
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Build a searchable, typed catalog of ‘microflows’ (small, composable admin/runbook fragments) with a synthesizer that compiles flow manifests into safe, executable task bundles. The catalog should let support engineers and automated systems discover, parameterize, dry-run, and execute repair flows with clear recovery checkpoints and provenance.

Motivation: Current runbook bits live in ad-hoc repos and notes. We need a machine-readable registry that captures signatures, preconditions, idempotency guarantees, safety gates, required privileges, and observability hooks so the Console can present curated, telemetry-rated repair options and the runtime can orchestrate mixed human+automated remediation.

Scope:
- Define flow manifest schema (inputs, outputs, preconditions, side-effect tags, rollback hooks, stability_score).
- Implement the catalog API (CRUD + search by tag/impact/required-role).
- Synthesizer: compile a manifest into a signed bundle containing runtime hints (batching affinity, expected tokens, KV cache warmup), a dry-run plan, and a rollback script.
- Integrate RBAC checks with Private deployment model and surface required privileges in Console.
- Add telemetry: execution trace, duration, success/failure reason, and a derived Stability Score used for UI ranking.
- Dry-run harness + simulated-replay for QA teams.

Key design decisions / trade-offs so far:
- Manifests are YAML-first (human-editable) but validated against a strict JSON Schema at ingest to avoid drift. Chose YAML for editability despite slightly more complex parsing.
- Bundle signing will use a per-environment key with short-lived attestations rather than a global master key to limit blast radius. This increases key management complexity but reduces risk on compromised dev machines.
- We will store only pointers to secrets (KMS references) in manifests; runtime will resolve via customer KMS/HSM integration. Adds latency during first-run but keeps manifests safe for audits.

Progress:
- Schema v0.1 drafted in docs: https://confluence.redwood.ai/ops/microflow-schema-v0.1 (internal).
- Prototype CLI tooling for manifest validation completed (branch: github.com/redwood-inference/ops-microflows/tree/feature/manifest-lint). PR #834 pending code review.
- Minimal catalog MVP API endpoints implemented behind feature flag: /catalog/list, /catalog/get, /catalog/validate. Service tests added.
- Console integration spike completed; mock UI shows catalog entries with Stability Score and required roles.

Open risks / blockers:
- KMS/HSM integration design needs security sign-off for Private deployments (blocking bundle signing flow).
- RBAC mapping across Dedicated vs Private must be reconciled with console auth model; design doc requires PM/SSO input.
- Run safety: we need deterministic idempotency patterns to avoid repeated side-effects when retries occur; ops has suggested adding explicit checkpoints.

Next steps (short term):
1) Address security review comments and finalize key rotation model (owner: security, target: 2025-03-07).
2) Land PR #834 (manifest validator, CLI) and publish schema to the docs site.
3) Implement bundle signing + attestations in the backend service; stub KMS calls for hosted and dedicated modes.
4) Hook telemetry events into the tracing pipeline and wire a Stability Score aggregator (telemetry infra ticket planned).
5) Create two sub-issues: one for the dry-run simulator harness and one for Console presentation improvements.

Acceptance criteria:
- Catalog API supports create/read/list/update/delete with JSON Schema validation.
- Synthesizer can produce a signed bundle and a dry-run plan that the simulator can execute without performing destructive changes.
- Console UI shows catalog entries with Stability Score and an action flow that runs dry-run then prompts for escalation to execute.
- Security sign-off on bundle signing and KMS resolution flow.

Links & references:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/ops/microflows-design (internal)
- Prototype CLI branch: github.com/redwood-inference/ops-microflows/tree/feature/manifest-lint
- Prototype Console mock: drive.google.com/drive/u/0/fake-microflows-mock

Notes for reviewers: focus on the manifest schema and the signing model. If we keep manifests expressive (custom scripting hooks) we risk safety; prefer a small set of allowed step types and parametrized commands.
